doc.title: Gordon Lorraine — Smithsonian Jazz Oral History

title: Ike Quebec and Art Blakey
summary: Ike Quebec was Blue Note's first musician friend and guide into Black jazz circles; he brought along Art Blakey.

story.theme_name: In the studio: making records, then and now
story.community_name: My first record date: sessions, personnel, discography

blocks.x: Good, you’re comfortable. So Ike Quebec...

Oh, yeah. What a dear man. Ike was I think the first friend that Blue Note Records really had as a musician and a friend. Most musicians were pals, but Ike was a friend. He was dear. And we loved his playing, because Alfred recorded him constantly, and I swooned because he had that great big sax sound. That’s so sexy. It was gorgeous. I thought Ike was the greatest. He never quite made it, unfortunately, but I still play his records today.
Art Blakey was also somebody who recorded early on with Blue Note as well.

Yeah. Well, these were all artists who were not even known outside of the small jazz...little whatever we were living in. It was a very small jazz world compared to junk or pop or crap that we have today. But Art was an up-and-coming drummer, and he was ferocious on the drums, and we loved him just for that. I think Ike brought him along. Ike was the mentor, in a way, for Alfred, by bringing us into areas of jazz that we had not been allowed to explore. There were great black musicians. Alfred was a great white entrepreneur, but Ike was a path for him. He was very generous in showing us around.
